issue.title: fix: PostMeltQuoteResponse.from_melt_quote uses `self` instead of `cls` and hardcodes class in @classmethod
issue.body: ## Summary `PostMeltQuoteResponse.from_melt_quote` is decorated with `@classmethod` but has two bugs: 1. The first parameter is named `self` instead of `cls`, which is misleading and inconsistent with Python classmethod conventions. 2. The method hardcodes `PostMeltQuoteResponse.model_validate(to_dict)` instead of using `cls.model_validate(to_dict)`, breaking correct behavior for any subclass that calls this method, it would silently return a `PostMeltQuoteResponse` instance instead of an instance of the subclass. This is inconsistent with `PostMintQuoteResponse.from_mint_quote` in `mint_quote.py`, which correctly uses `cls`. ## Expected behavior Calling `SubclassOfPostMeltQuoteResponse.from_melt_quote(quote)` should return an instance of the subclass, not of `PostMeltQuoteResponse`. ## Affected file `cashu/core/models/melt_quote.py` ## Screenshot of report

issue.title: fix(core): use cls instead of self in PostMeltResponse.from_melt_quote
issue.body:
## Fixes #1006

## Summary

`PostMeltQuoteResponse.from_melt_quote` was decorated with `@classmethod` but had two bugs:

- The first parameter was named `self` instead of `cls`, inconsistent with Python classmethod conventions.
- The return statement hardcoded `PostMeltQuoteResponse.model_validate(to_dict)` instead of `cls.model_validate(to_dict)`, silently returning a `PostMeltQuoteResponse` instance even when called on a subclass.

## Changes

- Renamed first parameter from `self` to `cls`
- Replaced `PostMeltQuoteResponse.model_validate(to_dict)` with `cls.model_validate(to_dict)`

This now matches the existing pattern in `PostMintQuoteResponse.from_mint_quote` in `cashu/core/models/mint_quote.py`.

issue.title: Bug: `UpdateQuoteTtl` writes to Redis cache TTL, not quote expiry
issue.body:
## Bug

The `UpdateQuoteTtl` gRPC method (defined in `management.proto` L177-183) accepts separate `mint_ttl` and `melt_ttl` fields, implying per-quote-type expiry control. However, the implementation in `management_rpc.py` L105-113 has two issues:

### 1. Wrong setting updated
Both fields write to `settings.mint_redis_cache_ttl`, which controls **Redis response cache duration** — not quote expiration. Quote expiry is actually derived from the Bolt11 invoice's own expiry timestamp at creation time and is unaffected by this RPC call.

```python
async def UpdateQuoteTtl(self, request, context):
    if request.mint_ttl:
        settings.mint_redis_cache_ttl = request.mint_ttl
    elif request.melt_ttl:
        settings.mint_redis_cache_ttl = request.melt_ttl
```

### 2. Both fields map to the same single setting
`mint_ttl` and `melt_ttl` both overwrite `settings.mint_redis_cache_ttl`. There is no way to set different values for mint vs melt. Additionally, due to `elif`, if both fields are provided in a single request, `melt_ttl` is silently ignored.

### Expected behavior
`UpdateQuoteTtl` should control how long mint/melt quotes remain valid (i.e., override or supplement the Bolt11-derived expiry), with independent settings for each quote type.

### Actual behavior
The method silently changes the Redis cache TTL instead, with no effect on quote expiration.

issue.title: feat(mint): enforce NUT 11014/11015 max inputs and outputs
issue.body:
This PR adds Cashu/NUT-aligned errors **11014** (*Max inputs exceeded*) and **11015** (*Max outputs exceeded*), configurable via **`MINT_MAX_INPUTS`** and **`MINT_MAX_OUTPUTS`** (defaults: 1000).

- Defines `TransactionMaxInputsExceededError` and `TransactionMaxOutputsExceededError` in `cashu/core/errors.py`.
- Enforces limits in `verify_inputs_and_outputs` and `_verify_outputs`, and on `restore()`.
- Aligns Pydantic request models so proof/input lists use the inputs cap and blinded output lists use the outputs cap.

Tests cover both error paths in `tests/mint/test_mint_verification.py`.

comment.body: The PR implements NUT-14 and NUT-15 limits on the maximum number of inputs and outputs by checking lengths and raising newly defined `TransactionMaxInputsExceededError` (11014) and `TransactionMaxOutputsExceededError` (11015). However, the PR also adds `max_length` validators to the Pydantic models for these endpoints. As a result, requests exceeding these limits are intercepted by FastAPI's Pydantic validation before reaching the route handlers, returning a generic HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity error instead of the protocol-specified Cashu 11014/11015 errors.

issue.title: get_blind_signatures_melt_id returns non-deterministic order
issue.body:
## get_blind_signatures_melt_id returns non-deterministic order

When a wallet checks a completed melt quote via GET /v1/melt/quote/bolt11/{id}, the change field contains blind signatures loaded from the promises table without an ORDER BY clause.

Also, it seems like maybe `get_blinded_messages_melt_id` in crud.py fetches the unsigned blinded messages from DB when reconstructing a quote response. These B_ values are then passed to `_generate_change_promises` which sorts amounts descending and assigns them to the DB-loaded messages. If they come back out of order, the wrong denominations get assigned to the wrong B_ values, producing mismatched signatures at the source. This means even the response from `get_melt_quote` can have wrong pairings.

The overall issue is that when reading from the db the ordering of outputs is not guaranteed and wallets expect the outputs to be in the same order as the blinded messages sent to the mint.

Related CDK issue: https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/issues/1933

issue.title: fix(mint): clean up pending proofs (NULL melt_quote) on mint startup
issue.body:
Follow up PR from https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/839

Pending proofs created during swap operations are written to `proofs_pending` with `melt_quote = NULL`. If the mint crashes mid-swap, these proofs are never cleaned up, the existing startup check only processes proofs that have an associated melt quote (i.e. outgoing Lightning payments).

## Changes

Extend `_check_pending_proofs_and_melt_quotes` to also query and remove pending proofs where `melt_quote IS NULL`. These are safe to delete on startup because:
-  if the mint is starting up, no swap is mid-flight
- Only melts involve an in-flight Lightning payment, and melts always write a non-NULL `melt_quote`

- A migration (`m034`) performs a one-time bulk cleanup of any existing orphaned rows for upgrading mints.

- `migrations.py`: `m034` deletes all `proofs_pending` rows with `melt_quote IS NULL`
- `crud.py`: adds `get_pending_proofs_without_melt_quote` query
- `ledger.py`: startup routine now unsets orphaned proofs after processing melt quotes
- `tests`: four new tests covering the cleanup logic and the query

forkee.description: Chaumian ecash wallet and mint for Bitcoin

issue.title: feat: support NUT-28 P2BK
issue.body:
Closes #856

## Summary
Implements NUT-28 (Pay-to-Blinded-Key) across Nutshell's core and wallet layers. P2BK extends NUT-11 (P2PK) spending conditions by ECDH-blinding each locking pubkey with an ECDH-derived scalar before the secret is written.  The mint sees a standard P2PK secret, enforces standard BIP-340 signatures, and learns nothing about the real receiver pubkey.

## What P2BK enables
- `Silent payments for Cashu` as sender locks ecash to a receiver pubkey without that pubkey ever appearing at the mint
- `Payment unlinkability` as each proof carries a fresh ephemeral pubkey E, making proofs from the same sender to the same receiver cryptographically unlinkable
- `True multi-party slots` as per-key ECDH means each pubkey in a multisig proof is independently blinded; slot owners cannot be linked or identified by position

## Changes
- Per-key ECDH in blind_pubkeys
- `p2pk_e` on Proof, `pe` on TokenV4Proof, V3/V4 serialization
- `create_p2bk_lock`, `_derive_p2bk_signing_key` with HTLC-safe try/except
- P2BK signing on swap + melt, HTLC inheritance comment, strip before mint
- P2BK: and P2BK-SIGALL: lock prefixes

comment.body: The Pay-to-Blinded-Key (NUT-28) implementation introduces an ephemeral public key (`p2pk_e`) which is critical for unblinding tokens. However, the wallet database schema and related `INSERT` statements were not updated to store the `p2pk_e` field. As a result, when a P2BK token is saved to the database and later retrieved (e.g., via the `cashu pending` command, or after a wallet restart), the `p2pk_e` field is permanently lost. This renders the generated token unspendable by the receiver and irrecoverable by the sender via refund paths, leading to a permanent loss of funds.
